head: Tiempo
Función
Ejemplo
rows: past simple
los sucesos, en orden
I opened the door and saw a man.
past continuous
el fondo, lo que estaba pasando
It was raining and the wind was blowing.
past perfect
lo que ya había pasado antes
Someone had broken the window.
past perfect continuous
cuánto tiempo llevaba pasando algo
He had been waiting for hours.

blocks.text: It was getting dark when I arrived at the station. I had been travelling all day and I was exhausted. When I looked for my ticket, I realised that I had left it on the train.

blocks.title: Del español al inglés
blocks.text: En una historia, el indefinido (abrí, vi) es el past simple; el imperfecto que describe el fondo (llovía, estaba lloviendo) es el past continuous; el pluscuamperfecto (había roto) es el past perfect; y llevaba horas esperando es el past perfect continuous. Pero el imperfecto de estados (estaba cansado, tenía hambre) va en past simple: I was tired.

Para costumbres y estados del pasado que ya no existen, se usa used to + verbo, como solía o el imperfecto: vivía en Sevilla = I used to live in Seville. Para acciones repetidas (no estados) también vale would.

head: Inglés
Español
rows: I used to live in Utrecht.
Antes vivía en Utrecht.
She didn't use to like coffee.
Antes no le gustaba el café.
Did you use to play football?
¿Jugabas al fútbol de pequeño?
Every summer we would go camping.
Todos los veranos íbamos de camping.

blocks.title: would no sirve para los estados
blocks.text: I used to have long hair está bien, I would have long hair no: tener, vivir, gustar y ser son estados. Y después de did y didn't se escribe use to, sin d. Ojo también: used to solo existe en pasado; para el presente, suelo levantarme es I usually get up.
3. be used to y get used to

head: Forma
Ejemplo
Significado
rows: used to + verbo
I used to drive on the right.
antes lo hacía
be used to + -ing
I'm used to driving on the left now.
estoy acostumbrado
get used to + -ing
I'm getting used to the cold.
me estoy acostumbrando

blocks.title: estar acostumbrado a = be used to + -ing
blocks.text: Después de be used to y get used to, to es una preposición, así que va seguido de -ing o de un sustantivo: I'm used to getting up early. I'm used to the noise. Nunca I'm used to get up, aunque en español digas acostumbrado a levantarme.

rows: Yesterday I have lost my keys.
Yesterday I lost my keys.
Un momento terminado: past simple.
When I arrived, the film already started.
When I arrived, the film had already started.
Lo que ya había pasado: past perfect.
I would have a dog when I was young.
I used to have a dog when I was young.
Un estado: used to.
Did you used to live here?
Did you use to live here?
Después de did: use to.
I'm used to get up early.
I'm used to getting up early.
be used to + -ing.
I use to play tennis as a child.
I used to play tennis as a child.
Antes, en el pasado: used to.
She was living here for ten years when she moved.
She had been living here for ten years when she moved.
Cuánto tiempo llevaba antes de un momento: had been + -ing.

blocks.text: Completa con la forma correcta. Las respuestas están en la última página.

items.q: While I ______ dinner, the phone rang.
items.full: While I was cooking dinner, the phone rang.

items.q: When we got to the cinema, the film ______.
items.full: When we got to the cinema, the film had started.

items.q: He was tired because he ______ all night.
items.full: He was tired because he had been working all night.

items.q: I ______ to live in a small village.
items.full: I used to live in a small village.

items.q: Did you ______ to have long hair?
items.full: Did you use to have long hair?

items.q: Every Sunday my grandfather ______ take us to the park.
items.full: Every Sunday my grandfather would take us to the park.

items.q: I'm not used to ______ on the left.
items.full: I'm not used to driving on the left.

items.q: You'll soon get used to ______ in a big city.
items.full: You'll soon get used to living in a big city.

items.q: She ______ her keys, so she couldn't get in.
items.full: She had lost her keys, so she couldn't get in.

items.q: The sun ______ and the birds were singing.
items.full: The sun was shining and the birds were singing.

items.a: I used to live in Utrecht.
I'm used to getting up early.

items.q: Cuando llegué, él ya se había ido.
items.a: When I arrived, he had already left.
